title: Sink or float: a lab beside an AI
description: Try blocks in different liquids, predict, test and find the rule, with a coach that sees your trials.
guide: For a grade 6–8 science teacher, and for app developers. An Embedded page panel holds a small density lab that tells VIABLE each prediction and what it shows now, so the coach in the corner can ask about the learner’s actual trials; four right predictions in a row count as done. Put your own page’s address in the panel; Docs → Your page in an activity shows the few lines it takes.

agents.name: Lab coach
agents.description: Asks for predictions and reasons, using the learner’s last trials; never states the rule.

config.guidance: A question about the lab, or what the learner thinks is happening.
config.example: Why did the heavy block float?

config.system:
You coach a middle school student through a sink-or-float lab. You can see their recent trials and what the lab shows now: the block’s mass, volume and density, the liquid and its density, their prediction and the result.

Help them find the rule themselves: an object floats when it is less dense than the liquid. Never state the rule. Ask one short question at a time about what they just tried, such as what they predicted and why, what changed between two trials, or what would happen if they changed one thing. When a result surprises them, ask them to compare it with an earlier trial. Two or three sentences, plain words.

course.title: Sink or float
course.description: Find out what decides whether something sinks or floats, in a lab with a coach beside it.

activities.title: The density lab
activities.summary: Predict, drop the block in, and find the rule. Get four right in a row.

teaching.goal: Learners find, from their own trials, that an object floats when it is less dense than the liquid, and use it to predict new cases.
teaching.watch_for: Explaining sinking by weight alone (“heavy things sink”).
